proposals.before: Some years later he was promoted to superintendent of waterways and parks, leapfrogging the commandant of justice.
proposals.after: Some years later he was promoted to superintendent of waterways and parks and was exceptionally appointed commandant of justice.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 超過廷尉 denotes exceptional advancement to the office of commandant of justice; the following text confirms that he served eighteen years in that office.

proposals.before: Some years later he was promoted superintendent of waterways and parks, passing over the commandant of justice.
proposals.after: Some years later he was promoted to superintendent of waterways and parks and was exceptionally appointed commandant of justice.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 超過廷尉 denotes exceptional advancement to the office of commandant of justice, not bypassing that office.

decisions.after: Several years later, he was promoted to Superintendent of Waterways and Parks, then advanced exceptionally to Commandant of Justice.
decisions.reason: 數年，遷水衡都尉，超過廷尉 pairs exceptional advancement (超, as in the preceding 超遷) with appointment as 廷尉, not skipping that office; later 為廷尉十八歲 and 于定國為廷尉 confirm he held it. The original “leapfrogging” invents a bypass.

decisions.after: Several years later, he was promoted to Superintendent of Waterways and Parks, then advanced exceptionally to Commandant of Justice.
decisions.reason: 超過廷尉 means he was exceptionally advanced to commandant of justice; “passing over” reverses the sense. The repair matches the Chinese offices and the exceptional-promotion idiom.
